世界洋流的分布规律与影响: Distribution and Effects of World Ocean Currents
盛行风 → 洋流 → 大洋环流（北顺南逆）: Prevailing winds → currents → ocean gyres (clockwise in the north, counterclockwise in the south)
数万只玩具鸭散落海面，为什么会漂到世界各地的海岸？: Tens of thousands of toy ducks were spilled at sea. Why did they drift to coasts all over the world?
盛行风吹拂 → 表层海水随风漂流: Prevailing winds blow → surface water drifts with the wind
遇陆地转向 → 中低纬成环（北顺南逆）: Turned by land → gyres in low and middle latitudes (clockwise north, counterclockwise south)
中高纬逆时针 · 西风漂流 · 季风洋流: Counterclockwise in middle-high latitudes · West Wind Drift · monsoon currents
按水温分寒暖 → 温度、盐度、密度: Warm or cold by water temperature → temperature, salinity, density
中低纬顺时针 · 中高纬逆时针 · 秘鲁上升流: Clockwise in low-middle latitudes · counterclockwise in middle-high latitudes · Peruvian upwelling
中低纬顺时针 · 中高纬逆时针: Clockwise in low-middle latitudes · counterclockwise in middle-high latitudes
南半球逆时针 · 北印度洋季风洋流: Counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere · monsoon currents in the northern Indian Ocean
海面上的水，为什么会自己走成一条条「河」？: Why does water on the sea surface move on its own in "rivers"?
拖动视角绕地球转一圈：海面上的洋流箭头，与它上方那一层更细的风箭头顶着同一个方向: Drag the globe all the way around: each current arrow on the sea surface points the same way as the finer wind arrow in the layer above it
赤道两侧：信风箭头向西，洋流箭头也向西（北赤道暖流 12°N→14°N，dLon: On either side of the equator the trade wind arrows point west and so do the current arrows (North Equatorial Current 12°N→14°N, dLon = −1); in the middle latitudes the westerly arrows point east and so do the current arrows (North Pacific Current 34°N→46°N, dLon = +1)
教材假设：地球表面均匀时，风向由气压带与风带决定: Textbook assumption: on a uniform Earth, wind direction is set by pressure belts and wind belts
盛行风吹拂海面，推动海水随风漂流，并使上层海水带动下层海水流动，在海洋表层形成规: Prevailing winds blow across the sea, making the water drift with the wind and dragging the lower layers along, forming large currents in the surface ocean.
洋流是「常年比较稳定地沿着一定方向作大规模的流动」，规模远超过河流的流量。: A current is "a large-scale flow that moves in a fairly stable direction year-round", far larger than any river's discharge.
洋流方向还受海陆分布、地转偏向力等因素影响：所以它并不总与风向完全一致。: Current direction is also affected by the distribution of land and sea and the Coriolis force, so it does not always match the wind exactly.
去掉这一步：只知道有水在流，不知道是谁在推，后面的每条规律都成了死记。: Skip this step and you only know water flows, not what pushes it, and every later pattern becomes rote memory.
常考：世界表层洋流的主要动力是盛行风；洋流方向还受海陆分布和地转偏向力影响。: Common exam point: the main driver of the world's surface currents is the prevailing wind; direction is also affected by land-sea distribution and the Coriolis force.
盛行风吹拂海面，推动海水随风漂流，在海洋表层形成规模很大的洋流；洋流方向还受海陆: Prevailing winds blow across the sea and make the water drift, forming large surface currents; current direction is also affected by land-sea distribution and the Coriolis force.
信风和西风都在推水，为什么中低纬会推成一个圈？: Trade winds and westerlies both push water. Why do they push it into a loop in low and middle latitudes?
把「洋流」滑块依次走过 北赤道暖流 → 日本暖流 → 北太平洋暖流 → 加利福尼: Move the "current" slider through North Equatorial Current → Kuroshio → North Pacific Current → California Current and see how the four arrows join end to end
北赤道暖流自东向西 → 撞上大洋西岸后沿西岸向北成日本暖流 → 到中纬被西风带成: The North Equatorial Current flows east to west → hits the western side of the ocean and turns north along it as the Kuroshio → in mid-latitudes the westerlies carry it east as the North Pacific Current → at the eastern side it turns back toward low latitudes, south, as the California Current → back to the equator, closing the loop: clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere (spinZ −1), and the center symbol turns clockwise; in the Southern Hemisphere the same winds push a counterclockwise loop (spinZ +1)
信风 + 西风 + 陆地阻挡 → 中低纬环流: Trade winds + westerlies + land barriers → low-middle latitude gyres
北半球顺时针 · 南半球逆时针: Clockwise in the north · counterclockwise in the south
西岸转向高纬: Turns poleward along the western side
信风把赤道两侧的海水自东向西推到大洋西岸，受陆地阻挡后，大部分海水沿西岸流向较高: The trade winds push water on both sides of the equator westward to the western side of the ocean; blocked by land, most of it flows along the western side toward higher latitudes.
到中纬度海区，在盛行西风吹拂下，洋流转为自西向东流；到大洋东岸又有一部分折向低纬: In the middle latitudes the prevailing westerlies turn the current eastward; at the eastern side part of it turns back toward low latitudes.
这样在中低纬海区闭合成大洋环流：北半球呈顺时针方向流动，南半球呈逆时针方向流动。: This closes an ocean gyre in the low-middle latitudes: clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
去掉这一步：只会背「北顺南逆」，说不出为什么；换一个半球就把方向画反。: Skip this step and you can only recite "clockwise north, counterclockwise south" without saying why, and draw the direction backward in the other hemisphere.
易错：北半球中低纬环流是顺时针、南半球中低纬是逆时针；北半球中高纬才是逆时针。: Common mistake: low-middle latitude gyres are clockwise in the north and counterclockwise in the south; only the northern middle-high latitude gyres are counterclockwise.
信风向西推、西风向东推，加上陆地阻挡，中低纬海区才闭合成大洋环流：北半球顺时针、: Trade winds push west and westerlies push east; with land barriers, the low-middle latitudes close into gyres: clockwise in the north, counterclockwise in the south.

中高纬反着转: Middle-high latitudes turn the other way
同在北半球，中高纬的环流为什么反着转？: Both in the Northern Hemisphere, why does the middle-high latitude gyre turn the other way?
把「洋流」滑块从墨西哥湾暖流拖到拉布拉多寒流，看环流中心那个弯箭头符号往哪边转: Drag the "current" slider from the Gulf Stream to the Labrador Current and see which way the curved arrow at the gyre's center turns
墨西哥湾暖流（24°N→40°N，向北）所在的中低纬环流顺时针（−1）；换成拉布: The Gulf Stream (24°N→40°N, northward) belongs to the clockwise low-middle latitude gyre (−1); switch to the Labrador Current (63°N→44°N, southward, ΔT −8.8 ℃) and its middle-high latitude gyre is counterclockwise (+1), opposite in sign; the East Greenland Current (72°N→60°N, ΔT −5.3 ℃) is in the same counterclockwise gyre, and the North Atlantic Current (44°N→62°N, ΔT +8.3 ℃) stays lit, since it is the edge shared by both gyres
极地东风 + 盛行西风 → 中高纬逆时针: Polar easterlies + prevailing westerlies → counterclockwise in middle-high latitudes
北半球中高纬：逆时针，与中低纬反号: Northern middle-high latitudes: counterclockwise, opposite to low-middle latitudes
在北半球中高纬度海区也形成大洋环流，它呈逆时针方向流动。: In the middle-high latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere ocean gyres also form, flowing counterclockwise.
原因在这一带的盛行风：北侧是极地东风（向西南吹），南侧是盛行西风（向东北吹），两: The reason is the prevailing winds there: polar easterlies on the north side (blowing southwest) and prevailing westerlies on the south side (blowing northeast) run in opposite directions, so the gyre's direction reverses.
千岛寒流（56°N→37°N，ΔT −8.5 ℃）、拉布拉多寒流、东格陵兰寒流都: The Oyashio (56°N→37°N, ΔT −8.5 ℃), the Labrador Current and the East Greenland Current are all in this counterclockwise gyre; the North Atlantic Current is the edge it shares with the low-middle latitude gyre (belongs to both), so it stays lit when you drag to the Labrador Current. The 3 cold currents of northern middle-high latitudes all have spinZ +1, opposite to the 8 low-middle latitude currents at −1.
去掉这一步：会以为整个北半球的洋流都朝同一个方向转。: Skip this step and you may think all currents in the Northern Hemisphere turn the same way.
常考：北半球中高纬大洋环流呈逆时针方向流动，与中低纬的顺时针相反。: Common exam point: northern middle-high latitude gyres flow counterclockwise, opposite to the clockwise low-middle latitude gyres.
北半球中高纬海区也形成大洋环流，呈逆时针方向流动——因为北侧极地东风向西、南侧盛: Gyres also form in the northern middle-high latitudes, flowing counterclockwise, because the polar easterlies on the north side blow west and the prevailing westerlies on the south side blow east, in opposite directions.

「暖流」「寒流」是按从低纬流向高纬分的吗？: Are "warm" and "cold" currents defined by flowing from low to high latitude?
把「洋流」滑块从墨西哥湾暖流拖到加那利寒流，盯住小读数里的 ΔT 和它的正负号: Drag the "current" slider from the Gulf Stream to the Canary Current, watching ΔT and its sign in the small readout
墨西哥湾暖流：源地 24°N 的表层水温比流经的 40°N 高 6.0 ℃（ΔT: Gulf Stream: surface water at its source (24°N) is 6.0 ℃ warmer than at 40°N where it flows (ΔT +6.0) → warm current; Canary Current: its source at 42°N is 8.5 ℃ colder than 18°N where it flows (ΔT −8.5) → cold current. The 10 zonal currents (North and South Equatorial Currents, Equatorial Countercurrents, Guinea Current, West Wind Drift and monsoon currents) show "zonal current · criterion not applicable", classed warm or cold by the textbook legend
ΔT = 源地水温 − 流经海区水温: ΔT = source water temperature − temperature of the area it flows through
ΔT > 0 → 暖流；ΔT < 0 → 寒流（教材按水温判）: ΔT > 0 → warm current; ΔT < 0 → cold current (the textbook judges by water temperature)
按海水温度，可以把洋流分为暖流和寒流：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域的洋流叫暖流: By water temperature, currents are warm or cold: a current flowing from warmer water to cooler water is a warm current, and the reverse is a cold current.
判据是两地的水温之差，不是「从低纬流向高纬」——那只是一种常见情形。: The criterion is the difference in water temperature between the two places, not "flowing from low to high latitude", which is only a common case.
洋流把水体本身搬走，水温随之平流，所以它给经过的海区加热或冷却；这正是暖流增温、: A current carries the water itself, and its temperature with it, so it warms or cools the areas it passes; that is why warm currents raise temperature and cold currents lower it.
去掉这一步：遇到西风漂流、季风洋流这类纬向流，就会按纬度方向把它们判错。: Skip this step and zonal currents such as the West Wind Drift and monsoon currents will be misjudged by their latitude direction.
易错：用「从低纬流向高纬」判暖流。正确判据是水温：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域: Common mistake: judging a warm current by "flows from low to high latitude". The correct criterion is water temperature: flowing from warmer water to cooler water = warm current.
寒暖按水温判：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域是暖流，反之是寒流；纬向流本课的温差: Warm or cold is judged by water temperature: from warmer to cooler water is a warm current, and the reverse a cold current; this lesson's temperature-difference criterion does not apply to zonal currents, which follow the textbook legend.
南半球的西风漂流为什么不绕圈？北印度洋的洋流为什么会倒过来流？: Why doesn't the West Wind Drift in the Southern Hemisphere form a loop? Why does the current in the northern Indian Ocean reverse?
把「月份」从 1 月拖到 7 月，盯住北印度洋那几条箭头和中心符号的转向: Drag "month" from January to July, watching the arrows in the northern Indian Ocean and the turn of the center symbol
北印度洋的季风洋流：1 月向西、逆时针（flowEW −1、spinZ +1）；: Monsoon currents of the northern Indian Ocean: westward and counterclockwise in January (flowEW −1, spinZ +1); eastward and clockwise in July (flowEW +1, spinZ −1), both signs flipping together; April and October show "transition" with no direction. On the same screen the Southern Hemisphere West Wind Drift (50°S–52°S, circling Antarctica, 13 vertices, net longitude +360°, flowEW +1) flows west to east all year and does not reverse with the seasons
季节风向反 → 北印度洋海水反向: Seasonal winds reverse → water in the northern Indian Ocean reverses
冬季向西逆时针 · 夏季向东顺时针: Westward and counterclockwise in winter · eastward and clockwise in summer
西风漂流不绕圈: The West Wind Drift does not loop
北印度洋海区冬季盛行东北风，海水向西流动、呈逆时针方向旋转；夏季盛行西南风，海水: In the northern Indian Ocean the northeast wind prevails in winter, so the water flows west and rotates counterclockwise; in summer the southwest wind prevails, so the water flows east and rotates clockwise.
南半球的西风漂流：南极大陆外围海面广阔，终年受西风影响，自西向东流动，教材没有给: The Southern Hemisphere West Wind Drift: the sea around Antarctica is vast and under westerlies all year, so the current flows west to east, and the textbook gives it no closed gyre.
两条都不成完整的圈，但原因不同：一条是海区被大陆半包围、盛行风随季节反向；一条是: Neither forms a complete loop, but for different reasons: one sea is half-enclosed by land with winds that reverse with the seasons; the other is open sea under westerlies all year.
去掉这一步：会把「南半球中高纬也有闭合大洋环流」和「北印度洋洋流全年朝一个方向」: Skip this step and you may wrongly remember both "the southern middle-high latitudes also have a closed gyre" and "the northern Indian Ocean current flows one way all year".
易错：北印度洋季风洋流方向记反——冬季东北风→向西→逆时针，夏季西南风→向东→顺: Common mistake: getting the monsoon current backward. Winter northeast wind → westward → counterclockwise; summer southwest wind → eastward → clockwise.
北印度洋的季风洋流随季风反向（冬季向西逆时针、夏季向东顺时针）；南半球的西风漂流: Monsoon currents of the northern Indian Ocean reverse with the monsoon (westward counterclockwise in winter, eastward clockwise in summer); the Southern Hemisphere West Wind Drift flows west to east around Antarctica all year and is not a closed gyre.
赤道的水最热，为什么盐度却不在赤道最高？: Equatorial water is the hottest. Why isn't salinity highest at the equator?
把「观察深度」拖到 1000 m，看第三个读数 T(z) 掉到哪里；再对着曲线看: Drag "observation depth" to 1000 m and see where the third reading T(z) drops to; then follow the curves for temperature and salinity versus latitude
8 月：表层水温随纬度递减 27.0 ℃（0°）> 24.4 ℃（25°N）>: August: surface water temperature falls with latitude, 27.0 ℃ (0°) > 24.4 ℃ (25°N) > 18.2 ℃ (45°N) > 12.5 ℃ (60°N); salinity peaks at 25° with 35.8 ‰ (0° 35.1 ‰, 60° 34.0 ‰); density rises from equator to poles, 1021.5 < 1023.7 < 1024.9 < 1025.8 kg·m⁻³; dragging depth at 25.75°N in the Kuroshio, T(z) goes 24.2 ℃ (0 m) → 9.7 ℃ (500 m) → 4.5 ℃ (1000 m), and falls only 1.5 ℃ more below 1000 m
温度 ↓ · 盐度副热带最高 · 密度 ↑: Temperature ↓ · salinity highest in the subtropics · density ↑
1000 m 以内变幅大、以下很小（教材 b1 p.50）: Large change within 1000 m, very little below (textbook b1 p.50)
由低纬向高纬递减: Decreases from low to high latitudes
全球海洋表层水温由低纬向高纬递减；同一海区的表层水温夏季普遍高于冬季（45°N: Surface ocean temperature decreases from low to high latitudes; in the same area surface water is generally warmer in summer than in winter (45°N rises from 14.5 ℃ to 18.2 ℃, 45°S falls from 18.5 ℃ to 14.7 ℃).
盐度以副热带海域最高，由副热带向赤道和两极逐渐降低：副热带炎热少雨、蒸发大于降水: Salinity is highest in the subtropics and decreases toward the equator and the poles: the subtropics are hot and dry with evaporation exceeding precipitation; the equator is hottest but has heavy rainfall.
密度由赤道向两极递增：表层海水密度与温度的关系最为密切，温度越高密度越低。: Density increases from the equator to the poles: surface density is most closely tied to temperature, and warmer water is less dense.
去掉这一步：会用「赤道最热所以盐度最高、密度最大」去推，这两条都错。: Skip this step and you may reason "the equator is hottest, so salinity and density are highest", both wrong.
常考：全球海洋表层海水的温度由低纬向高纬递减，盐度由副热带向两侧高低纬递减，密度: Common exam point: surface ocean temperature decreases from low to high latitudes, salinity decreases from the subtropics toward both higher and lower latitudes, and density increases from the equator to the poles.
水温由低纬向高纬递减；盐度以副热带最高、向赤道和两极降低；密度由赤道向两极递增；: Water temperature decreases from low to high latitudes; salinity is highest in the subtropics and lower toward the equator and poles; density increases from equator to poles; vertically, change is large within 1000 m and very small below.
A2.7.2–A2.7.4、A2.8.3、A2.8.6、A2.9.2、A4.5；: A2.7.2–A2.7.4, A2.8.3, A2.8.6, A2.9.2, A4.5; N1, N13; B2.1 ①②⑥; B2.2 tables 3 and 4 (August column)
同纬度的东岸和西岸，气候为什么差这么多？: Why do east and west coasts at the same latitude have such different climates?
把「洋流」滑块从加那利寒流拖到北大西洋暖流，看两岸读数与色斑怎样翻转: Drag the "current" slider from the Canary Current to the North Atlantic Current and see how the coastal readings and color patches flip
Same latitude comparison (55°N–70°N): the western coast of Labrador is affected by the Labrador Current (ΔT −8.8 ℃), with coastal air 9.6 ℃ colder; drag to the North Atlantic Current (44°N→62°N, ΔT +8.3 ℃) and the eastern coast of western Europe is 9.1 ℃ warmer, a difference of 18.8 ℃, within the textbook's "at 55°N–70°N, the coldest-month mean on the east side of the Atlantic is 16–20 ℃ higher than on the west" (the starting Canary Current, ΔT −8.5 ℃, lies further south off northwest Africa and is not part of this comparison). The Galápagos Islands on the equator (92°W) average about 24.7 ℃ with 578 mm of rain a year, cooler and drier than rainforest at the same latitude, because the Peru Current (ΔT −6.7 ℃) makes coastal air 7.4 ℃ colder
教材案例：东岸比西岸高 16—20 ℃: Textbook case: the east coast is 16–20 ℃ warmer than the west
暖流增温增湿: Warm currents add heat and moisture
暖流使所经海面及附近地区气温偏高、空气暖湿、对流加强，易形成降水；寒流相反：空气: Warm currents make the sea surface and nearby land warmer, with warm moist air and stronger convection that favors rain; cold currents do the opposite: stable air and little rain.
由于大洋东部和西部洋流性质不同，同纬度大洋东岸和西岸的气温存在差异。: Because currents on the eastern and western sides of an ocean differ, coasts at the same latitude on either side have different temperatures.
澳大利亚、非洲和南美洲西岸的热带沙漠气候，都与沿岸寒流有关；教材只给「偏高 /: The tropical desert climates on the western coasts of Australia, Africa and South America are all linked to coastal cold currents; the textbook only says "warmer / colder", and the factor of 1.1 for ΔT_air is the lesson's estimate.
去掉这一步：会把暖流对气候的影响说成「降温」，也会解释不了同纬度东西岸景观为什么: Skip this step and you may say warm currents "cool" the climate, and be unable to explain why east and west coasts at the same latitude look so different.
常考：暖流使沿岸气温偏高、降水增多；寒流使沿岸气温偏低、降水减少；大陆西岸热带沙: Common exam point: warm currents make coasts warmer and wetter; cold currents make them cooler and drier; tropical deserts on western continental coasts are linked to coastal cold currents.
暖流增温增湿、寒流降温减湿，同纬度大洋东西岸的气温与降水差异由此而来（教材案例：: Warm currents add heat and moisture and cold currents cool and dry, which explains the differences in temperature and rainfall between east and west coasts at the same latitude (textbook case: the coldest month on the east side is 16–20 ℃ warmer than on the west).

Near Newfoundland (48°N, 50°W) the Labrador Current meets the Gulf Stream; the textbook's Newfoundland fishery has banned cod fishing since 1992
离岸风 / 交汇 → 营养盐上涌 → 渔场: Offshore wind / convergence → nutrients rise → fishery
寒流和暖流交汇处海水扰动强烈，沉积于海底的营养物质上涌，浮游生物繁盛，鱼类聚集，: Where cold and warm currents meet, the water is strongly stirred, nutrients from the seabed rise, plankton thrives, fish gather, and a great fishing ground forms.
秘鲁沿海在东南信风吹拂下表层海水偏离海岸，深部冷水带着海底的营养物质上涌，也形成: Off Peru the southeast trade winds push surface water away from the coast, and cold deep water rises with seabed nutrients, forming another world-famous fishery.
大渔场的关键是营养盐上涌，不是「水温合适」；纽芬兰渔场 20 世纪 50 年代过: The key to a great fishery is rising nutrients, not "the right water temperature"; after overfishing in the 1950s the Newfoundland stocks collapsed, and Canada banned cod fishing in 1992.

常考：大渔场的成因——寒暖流交汇、离岸风上升流，本质都是把营养盐带到有光层。: Common exam point: causes of great fisheries — warm-cold convergence and offshore-wind upwelling, both of which bring nutrients into the sunlit layer.
